To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the amount of academic words used in student essays is positively related to perceived quality of the essays in some text types and 2) academic vocabulary use is influenced by rhetorical purposes and text types, independent of the draft.
the use of academic language varies according to the rhetorical purpose of the writing task.
academic vocabulary use in student papers is influenced by rhetorical purposes and that there is little difference between drafts in academic vocabulary use.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how students use academic vocabulary in their writing and what factors influence that use.
the role that academic vocabulary plays in the writing process of ESL students.
academic vocabulary in the classroom, and the results have important implications for teaching academic writing and assessing academic language proficiency.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of academic word lists in ESL writing classrooms should be carefully considered and that the focus on academic words should be integrated in the writing process and the rhetorical goals of the writing tasks.
the use of academic language in writing is not only a matter of the amount of academic words employed, but also the way they are used.

the use of academic word vocabulary is a complex phenomenon, and that a more in depth analysis of the relationship between academic vocabulary use, text type, and rhetorical purposes is necessary to fully understand how students use this vocabulary.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
academic vocabulary use is an important component of student writing, but that it is not a panacea to writing quality.
academic vocabulary is used differently across text types and drafts, but that it can still be taught and learned in a writing classroom.

the use of academic language in student essays is not a simple matter, and that the use of these words is influenced by the rhetorical purposes of the text, the text type, and the level of instruction, independent from the drafts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the way students use academic vocabulary varies across text types, drafts, and writing levels.

students are using academic vocabulary in ways that are consistent with the rhetorical purposes of the text, but that they may not be using them in ways that are appropriate for the level of instruction.
academic vocabulary use is a complex phenomenon that needs to be studied in relation to rhetorical purposes and other factors that affect academic writing.
